newsitem.title: UK: CU Euro-growth offsets weather loss.
newsitem.headline: CU Euro-growth offsets weather loss.

text.p: LONDON - British insurer Commercial Union on Wednesday reported a slide in nine month operating profits, but strong growth in continental Europe helped to offset the effects of increased weather losses in the United States and Britain.

Nine month operating pre-tax profits fell to 348 million pounds ($575.2 million) from 384 million. But CU noted that a strong performance from its business in France and the Netherlands helped to counter a 62 million pound increase in weather claims.
The company also said it was hopeful of setting up a life assurance operation in the Czech Republic early next year.

"A strong third quarter result, with pre-tax operating profits broadly similar to last year, led to a good underlying performance at the nine months stage, in spite of the substantial increase in weather claims earlier in the year," chief executive John Carter said in a statement.
"Increased profits were achieved in France and the Netherlands and our life operations continued to make good progress with strong growth in new business."

In Britain, where oversupply and the advent of direct selling techniques have intensified competition among insurers and dragged rates lower over the last two to three years, CU's general insurance premium income fell by 12 percent.
"The rating environment remains competitive, although there are signs of competition reducing in the motor classes," the company said of the British market.

Much of the attention paid to the industry in Britain has focused on the direction of prices, and personal motor insurance rates in particular. These have been in decline but some insurers say they now appear to be bottoming out.
Finance director Peter Foster said in an interview that CU had not made any rating increases but had not reduced rates by as much as other insurers when prices were falling.
The next move from CU on rates would probably be in an upward direction.
Foster said the company applied several weeks ago to the Czech Republic's finance ministry for permission to set up a life assurance business.
If the company is granted approval shortly, it may establish the operation sometime during the early part of 1997.
The amount invested initially would be small, said Foster, but the potential for rapid growth is significant. Poland is currently the group's fastest growing territory.
CU announced its results the day after French insurers Axa and UAP unveiled plans to merge creating a world insurance giant, but it is not inclined to seek economies of scale through such a merger.

"Size for size's own sake we don't regard as desirable. If you're an efficient company with reasonable scale, one can actually be pretty efficient and we continue to have one of the best ratios as far as the UK is concerned," said Foster.

"There aren't very many opportunities that arise where one can see the quality of the business for the right price being available. We keep our eyes open, but organic growth is something we feel we've been quite successful at in the past."
CU shares were eight pence up at 647 after touching a high of 652. -- London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7721 ($1=.6050 Pound)
